        "anchor": "stmt-prop-two-families",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the constants $D_0$ and $C_{\\mathrm{tpl}}$ in Definition <a href=\"#scanner:template\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"scanner:template\">27</a>, and a lower scale threshold $n_*\\ge1$. There is a constant $C$ with the following property. Let $\\Lambda$ be a finite induced subgraph of the square lattice, let $A\\subseteq\\Lambda$, and suppose that $b=|\\partial_\\Lambda A|>0$. Let $Z$ be the set of endpoints of those cut edges.*\n\n*There are a set $D\\subseteq A$, a finite ordered collection of disjoint nonempty sets $X_i\\subseteq A$, labels $f_i\\in\\{0,1\\}$, ambient templates $T_i\\subset\\mathbb Z^2$, and integers $n_i\\ge n_*$ such that:*\n\n1.  *$A=D\\mathbin{\\dot\\cup}\\bigcup_iX_i$ and $|D|\\le Cb$.*\n\n2.  *$X_i\\subseteq A\\cap T_i$. Each $T_i$ is a template of Definition <a href=\"#scanner:template\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"scanner:template\">27</a>: it is a union of $N_i$ lattice samples of closed convex rectangles or triangles with side slopes $0,\\infty,1,-1$, each of sup-norm diameter at most $s_i$, where $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{diam}}_\\infty T_i\\le n_i,\\qquad\n     n_i\\ge C_{\\mathrm{tpl}}N_i(s_i+1),\\qquad\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}_\\infty(T_i,Z)>4D_0s_i.$$ Moreover $L_i=\\lfloor n_i^{1-\\ell}\\rfloor\\le s_i$.*\n\n\n\n3.  *The templates satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}_\\infty(T_i,Z)&>2n_i^\\beta,\\label{geometry:cut-clearance}\\\\\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{dist}}_\\infty\\left(T_i,\n           \\bigcup_{\\substack{j<i\\\\f_j=f_i}}X_j\\right)\n           &>2n_i^\\beta.\\label{geometry:ordered-clearance}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ As usual, the distance to the empty set is infinite.*\n\n4.  *The scale losses are summable: $$\\sum_i n_i^{-100}\\le Cb.$$*\n\n*The constant $C$ may depend on the fixed template constants and on $n_*$, but not on the domain or cut.",

        "exact_quote": "For a sufficiently small fixed choice of $a_0$ and the corresponding threshold $S_*$, every active mark $(v,S)$ at every generation has a terminal-square-free isolated star $v+[-a_0S,a_0S]^2$ with the properties of Lemma <a href=\"#geometry:initial-stars\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"geometry:initial-stars\">35</a>. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Induced square-lattice domain and graph distance** ([source](#eq:hamiltonian)): Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2$ be finite. Its edges join pairs at Euclidean distance one, so that $\Lambda$ carries the induced square-lattice graph. Write $d_\Lambda$ for graph distance, with value $+\infty$ between different components.
- **Admissible finite-range Hamiltonian** ([source](#eq:hamiltonian)): An admissible Hamiltonian has the form $$\label{eq:hamiltonian} H=\sum_{\substack{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\Lambda\\ \mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{d_\Lambda}X\le R}}h_X, \qquad h_X=h_X^*,\qquad \lVert h_X\rVert\le J.$$
- **Edge boundary** ([source](#pm-h-3)): For $A\subseteq\Lambda$ define the edge boundary $$\partial_\Lambda A= \{\{x,y\}:x\in A,\ y\in\Lambda\setminus A,\ \|x-y\|_1=1\}.$$
- **Ground-vector marginal and entanglement entropy** ([source](#pm-h-3)): If $\Omega\in\mathcal H_\Lambda$ is a unit vector, write $\rho_A=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\Lambda\setminus A}\lvert \Omega\rangle\langle \Omega\rvert$ and $S_\Omega(A)=-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\rho_A\log\rho_A$, with $0\log0=0$.
- **Conditional entropy and information quantities** ([source](#pm-h-8)): For a density matrix $\rho$ on systems $D,E,F$, define $$S(D\|E)_\rho=S(DE)_\rho-S(E)_\rho, \quad I(D:E)_\rho=S(D)_\rho+S(E)_\rho-S(DE)_\rho,$$ and $$I(D:F\|E)_\rho=S(DE)_\rho+S(EF)_\rho-S(E)_\rho-S(DEF)_\rho.$$
- **Safe rectangle** ([source](#pm-h-12)): We call $Q$ *safe* if $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(Q,Z)>D_0\,\operatorname{size}(Q),$$ with distance to the empty set taken to be infinite.
- **Safe-box entropy supremum** ([source](#pm-h-17)): For an integer $r\ge1$, let $F_{\mathrm{box}}(r)$ be the supremum of $S_\Omega(A\cap Q)$ over all admissible Hamiltonians and cuts with fixed $q,R,J,\Delta$, and all safe integer rectangles $Q$ of size at most $r$.
- **Normalized graph-ball conditional expectation** ([source](#eq:quasilocal-ce)): The normalized conditional expectation onto this ball is the map $$E_{i,l}(B)=q^{-\|\Lambda\setminus N_l(a_i)\|} \mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\Lambda\setminus N_l(a_i)}(B) \otimes I_{\Lambda\setminus N_l(a_i)}. \label{eq:quasilocal-ce}$$
- **Support powers and unitary kernel extension** ([source](#sec:conditional)): For a density matrix $\rho$, write $$\rho^{[z]}=\sum_{p>0}p^z\Pi_p, \qquad \widehat\rho=\rho+\Pi_{\ker\rho}.$$
- **Symmetric replica space** ([source](#sec:replicas)): Write $$d=\dim\mathcal V,\qquad \mathcal S_k=\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^k\mathcal V,\qquad D_k=\dim\mathcal S_k=\binom{k+d-1}{d-1},$$ and let $\Pi_k$ be the orthogonal projector onto $\mathcal S_k$.
- **Schur-label observable** ([source](#pm-h-28)): Define the self-adjoint label observable $$\label{replicas:F-definition} F_{Q,k}=\sum_{\lambda\vdash k}(\log d_\lambda)\pi_{Q,k}^{\lambda}.$$
- **Partition leaf metric** ([source](#replicas:leaf-metric)): Define the partition’s metric on $\mathcal S_k$ by $$\label{replicas:leaf-metric} A_k(P,Y,F)=\bigl(W_{P,k}^{-1}W_{F,k}^{-1}W_{Y,k}\bigr)^2.$$
- **Coherent probability measure** ([source](#pm-h-31)): For a density matrix $\sigma$ supported on $\mathcal S_k$, define its coherent probability measure by $$\label{replicas:husimi} d\mu_\sigma(\theta)=D_k\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}(\sigma P_{\theta,k})\,d\theta.$$
- **Weighted operator geometric mean** ([source](#transport:mean-def)): For positive definite operators $A,B$ on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and $0\leq p\leq1$, define $$\label{transport:mean-def} A\#_p B=A^{1/2}(A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2})^pA^{1/2}.$$
- **Template** ([source](#stmt-scanner-template)): Let $s_0\ge1$ and $n$ be positive integers. A template with parameters $(n,s_0)$ is a nonempty finite set $T\subset\mathbb Z^2$ of the form $$T=\bigcup_{a=1}^{N_0}(P_a\cap\mathbb Z^2), \qquad n\ge C_{\rm tpl}N_0(s_0+1), \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_\infty T\le n,$$ where $N_0\ge1$ is an integer and each $P_a$ is a closed convex rectangle or triangle of sup-norm diameter at most $s_0$, all of whose sides have slope $0,\infty,1$, or $-1$. Empty sampled pieces can be omitted. For the fixed cut $A$, the template is separated from the cut if $$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_\infty(T,Z)>4D_0s_0.$$ As above, $T_j$ is the ambient integer dilation, $X=A\cap T$, and $Q_j=A\cap(T_j\setminus T)$, for $j\ge0$.
- **Birth region and actual region** ([source](#pm-h-61)): A *birth region* below is the bounded closed planar region assigned to a tile when that tile is created. Later steps only delete points from that tile. Its *actual region* is the interior of its birth region remaining after all deletions.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-controlled-continuity** [claim](#stmt-lem-continuity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-continuity): Jordan decomposition and conditional-entropy mixture bounds. -> Entropy perturbation bounds independent of spectator dimension.
- **step-component-factorisation** [claim](#stmt-lem-zero-boundary) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-zero-boundary): Tensor-sum decomposition over graph components and ground-space uniqueness. -> Vanishing entropy across an empty boundary.
- **step-surprisal-tails** [claim](#stmt-lem-tail) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-tail): Marginal tilting, narrow-strip interpolation, quadratic real-part control and the full-system gap. -> Marginal moment and tail bounds.
- **step-buffer-discount** [claim](#stmt-lem-initial-buffer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-initial-buffer): Optimize nested positive filters, bound their energy and compare with Schmidt-pinned trials. -> A conditional-entropy discount across a buffer.
- **step-initial-box-recursion** [claim](#stmt-prop-initial-box) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-initial-box): Average entropy chains over child orders and iterate the resulting scale recursion. -> An initial entropy exponent below volume.
- **step-graph-propagation** [claim](#stmt-lem-quasilocal-lr) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-quasilocal-lr): Iterate the commutator integral inequality and telescope exterior on-site twirls. -> Graph-distance propagation and conditional-expectation tails.
- **step-filter-decay** [claim](#stmt-lem-quasilocal-filter) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-quasilocal-filter): Cauchy derivative estimates and optimized integration by parts. -> Exact spectral cutoff with stretched-exponential time decay.
- **step-positive-replacement** [claim](#stmt-prop-positive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-positive): Center filtered interactions and take their absolute values. -> Positive ground-state-annihilating constraints retaining the gap.
- **step-root-channels** [claim](#stmt-lem-quasilocal-roots) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-quasilocal-roots): Square-root order estimates and Kraus-isometry contractivity. -> Local root approximants and unital completely positive channels.
- **step-volume-free-truncation** [claim](#stmt-prop-truncation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-truncation): Sum distance-dependent tails near the testing set and apply spectral perturbation bounds. -> A local testing Hamiltonian with controlled ground vector and cut budgets.
- **step-conditional-movement** [claim](#stmt-lem-movement) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-movement): Conditional Schatten interpolation with retained Hölder slack and continuity. -> A norm contraction governed by conditional information.
- **step-phase-comparison** [claim](#stmt-lem-conditional-phases) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-conditional-phases): Integrate a nonnegative resolvent defect and control the integral endpoints by dimension moments. -> A dimension-controlled marginal-phase discrepancy.
- **step-local-skew** [claim](#stmt-lem-skew) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-skew): Combine phase comparison, narrow-strip bounds and Cauchy estimates. -> Real-power scalar skew bounded by conditional information.
- **step-schur-labels** [claim](#stmt-lem-schur) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-schur): Schur–Weyl decomposition, character formulas, subgroup restriction and removable-row branching. -> Dimension, surprisal and marked-copy label estimates.
- **step-common-metric** [claim](#stmt-replicas-metric) / [proof](#proof-stmt-replicas-metric): Simplex gamma integration, subsystem compression and marked gamma-ratio asymptotics. -> Common central metrics, tensor-power mixtures and symmetric inverse bounds.
- **step-relative-pin** [claim](#stmt-lem-relative-pin) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-relative-pin): Expand metric mixtures, apply the one-copy movement estimate and invert a quadratic-form bound. -> A conditional-information lower pin for a subsystem move.
- **step-symbol-products** [claim](#stmt-lem-symbol) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-symbol): Clip inverse ratios, approximate by polynomial star words and separate copy placements before taking absolute values. -> Uniform polynomial and absolute-value scalar symbols.
- **step-mean-tree-properties** [claim](#stmt-transport-means) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transport-means): Operator-monotone power integrals and induction through the specified binary tree. -> Root monotonicity, vector bounds and projection transfer.
- **step-positive-derivative-maps** [claim](#stmt-transport-cp) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transport-cp): Differentiate the power integral and normalize using scalar homogeneity. -> Unital completely positive leaf-to-root maps.
- **step-fourier-kernels** [claim](#stmt-transport-fourier) / [proof](#proof-stmt-transport-fourier): Residue calculation and pole-free contour shifts. -> A positive norm-derivative density and bounded energy densities.
- **step-common-state-transport** [claim](#stmt-prop-transport) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-transport): Transport relative pins through logarithmic Jensen bounds and energy squares through auxiliary block trees. -> Coupled entropy-gain and energy estimates in the same transported states.
- **step-norm-comparators** [claim](#stmt-prop-comparators) / [proof](#pm-h-46): Select auxiliary Schur labels, Bell-pin the target and bound inverse metrics on sectors with few excited copies. -> Rough and sharp norm comparisons and the physical entropy identity.
- **step-scanner-histories** [claim](#stmt-scanner-histories) / [proof](#proof-stmt-scanner-histories): Use fixed fill fronts, random offsets and charge ancestry bounds. -> Controlled status geometry, split dilution and good-history sampling.
- **step-scanner-selection** [claim](#stmt-prop-scanner) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-scanner): Telescope integrated entropy derivatives and average over charge rounds and the common interpolation parameter. -> A selected interpolation with small defect energy and uniform comparator data.
- **step-template-coverings** [claim](#stmt-scanner-templates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-scanner-templates): Count polygonal depth rows and maximal contained dyadic squares. -> Core and shell entropy inputs with controlled physical boundaries.
- **step-safe-box-bootstrap** [claim](#stmt-prop-small-box) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-small-box): Apply the rough comparisons at selected scanner points and iterate the exponent discount finitely. -> The improved safe-box exponent.
- **step-collar-bound** [claim](#stmt-prop-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-collar): Use growing total metric weight in sharp comparisons and discard to the fixed far subsystem. -> Sublinear collar mutual information in the original ground state.
- **step-local-clock-products** [claim](#stmt-lem-amplification-local-products) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-amplification-local-products): Propagate on-site oscillations under unital channels and telescope coupled full and retained clock products. -> Volume-independent expected omission and truncation errors.
- **step-information-amplification** [claim](#stmt-prop-amplification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-amplification): Construct a typical restoring operator, suppress its excited component on a good clock realization and extend its polar factor to a local unitary. -> Arbitrary inverse-power remote mutual information.
- **step-entropy-cancellation** [claim](#stmt-geometry-cancellation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geometry-cancellation): Add the entropy-chain inequalities for the ordered families and use purity. -> Cancellation of all individual tile entropies.
- **step-initial-contact-stars** [claim](#stmt-geometry-initial-stars) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geometry-initial-stars): Inspect the translated fine mesh and its finite allowed line arrangement. -> Uniform mark separation and isolated radial stars.
- **step-recursive-contact-repair** [claim](#stmt-geometry-repair-induction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geometry-repair-induction): Remove disjoint squares from all old identifiers, reverse sector labels and induct on shrinking scales. -> Uniform recursive separation, descendant confinement and termination.
- **step-birth-template-separation** [claim](#stmt-geometry-birth-separation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-geometry-birth-separation): Combine compactness of finite rescaled patterns with angular separation after trimming older contact regions. -> Birth-template clearance from earlier and peer same-label actual regions.
- **step-geometric-families** [claim](#stmt-prop-two-families) / [proof](#pm-h-66): Build distance layers and sparse belts, repair contacts, count descendants and assign template scales. -> Ordered separated families with boundary-sized exceptions and summable scale losses.
- **step-area-law-assembly** [claim](#stmt-thm-area) / [proof](#pm-h-67): Apply collar amplification to each birth template and cancel the region entropies. -> Uniform entropy area law for arbitrary physical subsets.
- **step-vertex-boundary-corollary** [claim](#stmt-cor-rectangles) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-rectangles): Count crossing-edge incidences at inner vertices and endpoints. -> Rectangular and vertex-boundary formulations.

          "exact_quote": "The entire finite physical system, $n$, the scan, and all auxiliary dimensions are fixed before $k\\to\\infty$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "scanner:selected-density",
          "exact_quote": "Averaging therefore gives a charge round and a $p_k$ in this interval such that $$\\frac{\\mathcal Q(p_k)}{KnD}\\le\\delta_n+o_k(1).\n \\label{scanner:selected-density}$$",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }
      ],
      "reason": "Averaging selects a round and parameter that may depend on the replica count. The proof needs uniform remainders to pass to the copy limit and does not supply a finite search complexity.",
      "step_id": "step-scanner-selection"
    },
    {
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "eq:amplification-good-trajectory",
          "exact_quote": "Markov’s inequality and a union bound consequently provide a realization satisfying $$\\label{eq:amplification-good-trajectory}\n \\|D(I-P_\\Omega)\\zeta\\|\\le n^{-K},\\quad\n \\|(D-D_{\\rm ret})\\zeta\\|\\le n^{-K},\\quad\n M_0\\|D_{\\rm ret}-L'\\|\\le n^{-K}.$$",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }
      ],
      "reason": "A Markov and union-bound argument selects a suitable clock realization. The resulting local unitary proves decoupling, without an efficient construction guarantee.",
      "step_id": "step-information-amplification"
    },
    {
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "geometry:belt-count",
          "exact_quote": "Hence some shift satisfies $$\\label{geometry:belt-count}\n \\#\\{\\text{belt cells in }D_k\\}\n \\le Cb\\frac{r^2}{s_kt_k}\n \\le Cb\\,2^{-k\\delta_0/2}.$$",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "geometry:fine-clearance",
          "exact_quote": "Finally increase $k_0$ to ensure that initial belt scales exceed $S_*$, that all primary scales exceed $n_*$, and that all the uniform large-scale inequalities just used hold.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }
      ],
      "reason": "Sparse belt shifts are chosen by averaging, and thresholds are made sufficiently large using asymptotic exponent gaps. The proof gives a finite decomposition for each domain without a stated computational complexity.",
      "step_id": "step-geometric-families"
    }

          "exact_quote": "Let $\\rho,\\sigma$ be density operators on finite-dimensional $D\\otimes E$, and put $\\delta=\\tfrac12\\lVert \\rho-\\sigma\\rVert_1\\le1$ and $d_D=\\dim D$. Then $$\\label{eq:conditional-continuity}\n |S(D|E)_\\rho-S(D|E)_\\sigma|\n \\le2\\delta\\log d_D+(1+\\delta)\n                 h\\left(\\frac{\\delta}{1+\\delta}\\right)\n \\le C\\sqrt\\delta\\log(e d_D).$$ The same estimates hold for $S(D)$ by making $E$ trivial. Summing the bounds for $S(D)$ and $S(D|E)$ therefore bounds the continuity cost for $I(D:E)$ in terms of $d_D$, independently of $\\dim E$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-tail",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal H=\\bigotimes_{v\\in V}\\mathcal H_v$ be a finite tensor product of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Let $\\mathsf H=\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal I} h_i$, where $\\mathcal I$ is finite, each $h_i$ is self-adjoint, $\\lVert h_i\\rVert\\le c_0$ for a fixed $c_0\\ge0$, and $h_i$ has a designated support $D_i\\subseteq V$. Suppose that $\\mathsf H$ has a one-dimensional ground space spanned by a normalized vector $\\Psi$, ground energy $E_0$, and gap at least $g_0>0$. Fix a bipartition $B\\sqcup B^c=V$. Let $\\mathcal I_\\times$ be the indices whose designated support meets both sides, and put $$\\rho=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Tr}}_{B^c}\\lvert \\Psi\\rangle\\langle \\Psi\\rvert,\\qquad\n d_i=\\prod_{v\\in D_i}\\dim\\mathcal H_v,\\qquad\n \\mathcal B=1+\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal I_\\times}\\log^2(\\mathrm e d_i).$$ Let $p_j$ be the positive eigenvalues of $\\rho$, let $K$ take the value $-\\log p_j$ with probability $p_j$, and write $S=S(\\rho)$ and $\\vartheta=c_0/g_0$. Then $$\\log\\mathbb E\\mathrm e^{uK}\n \\le uS+512\\mathrm e\\,\\vartheta\\mathcal B u^2,\n \\qquad\n |u|\\le\\frac{1}{32\\sqrt{(1+\\vartheta)\\mathcal B}}.\n \\label{eq:initial-tail-mgf}$$ Consequently, for every $w\\ge0$, $$\\Pr\\{|K-S|>w\\}\n \\le \\min\\left\\{1,\\,\n  2\\mathrm e^{\\mathrm e/2}\n  \\exp\\left(-\\frac{w}{32\\sqrt{(1+\\vartheta)\\mathcal B}}\\right)\n              \\right\\}.\n \\label{eq:initial-tail-probability}$$",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-quasilocal-lr",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\tau_t(B)=e^{itH}Be^{-itH}$. There are positive constants $C,v,c$ such that, for every original support $X_i$, every operator $A$ supported in $X_i$, every site $y$, and every on-site operator $B_y$, $$\\|[\\tau_t(A),B_y]\\|\n \\le C\\|A\\|\\|B_y\\|e^{v|t|-c d_\\Lambda(a_i,y)}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-lr}$$ The commutator is zero when $d_\\Lambda(a_i,y)=\\infty$. Moreover, $$\\|\\tau_t(A)-E_{i,l}(\\tau_t(A))\\|\n \\le \\|A\\|\\min\\{2,Ce^{v|t|-cl}\\}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-lr-ce}$$",

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-quasilocal-filter",
          "exact_quote": "Fix an integer $p\\ge1$, put $\\alpha=p/(p+1)$, and let $\\delta>0$. Define the real even function $$\\chi(\\omega)=\n \\begin{cases}\n  e\\exp[-(1-(\\omega/\\delta)^2)^{-p}],&|\\omega|<\\delta,\\\\\n  0,&|\\omega|\\ge\\delta.\n \\end{cases}$$ Then $\\chi\\in C_c^\\infty(\\mathbb R)$, $\\chi(0)=1$, and the real even function $$f(t)=\\frac1{2\\pi}\\int_{\\mathbb R}\\chi(\\omega)e^{-it\\omega}\\,d\\omega$$ satisfies $$\\chi(\\omega)=\\int_{\\mathbb R}f(t)e^{it\\omega}\\,dt,\n \\qquad |f(t)|\\le Ce^{-c|t|^\\alpha}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-filter-decay}$$ Here $C,c>0$ depend only on $p,\\delta$.",

      "claim_anchor": "stmt-prop-positive",
      "depends_on": [

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-positive",
          "exact_quote": "Suppose $H\\Omega=E_0\\Omega$, $\\|\\Omega\\|=1$, and $$H-E_0I\\ge\\Delta(I-P_\\Omega),\\qquad\n P_\\Omega=|\\Omega\\rangle\\langle\\Omega|.$$ For each integer $p\\ge1$ and $\\alpha=p/(p+1)$, there are operators $k_i$, indexed by the original supports and retaining their anchors, and a constant $c_*>0$ such that $$0\\le k_i\\le I,\\qquad k_i\\Omega=0,\\qquad\n H_F:=\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal I}k_i\n       \\ge c_*^{-1}(H-E_0I)\\ge g(I-P_\\Omega),\n \\qquad g:=\\Delta/c_*.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-positive}$$ Thus $H_F$ has the unique ground vector $\\Omega$, ground energy zero, and gap at least $g$. Furthermore, $$k_{i,l}:=E_{i,l}(k_i)\\in[0,I],\\qquad\n \\|k_i-k_{i,l}\\|\\le Ce^{-cl^\\alpha}\n \\quad(l\\in\\mathbb Z_{\\ge0}).\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-positive-tail}$$ Each $k_i$ is supported in the connected component containing $a_i$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-quasilocal-roots",
          "exact_quote": "For the constraints of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:positive\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:positive\">10</a>, define $$G_i=(I-k_i)^{1/2},\\quad K_i=k_i^{1/2},\\qquad\n G_{i,l}=(I-k_{i,l})^{1/2},\\quad K_{i,l}=k_{i,l}^{1/2}.$$ These are positive contractions, $G_i\\Omega=\\Omega$, $K_i\\Omega=0$, and $$\\|G_i-G_{i,l}\\|+\\|K_i-K_{i,l}\\|\\le Ce^{-cl^\\alpha},\n \\qquad G_{i,l}^2+K_{i,l}^2=I.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-root-tail}$$ Define maps on the full operator algebra by $$\\mathcal E_i(B)=G_iBG_i+K_iBK_i,\\qquad\n \\mathcal E_{i,l}(B)=G_{i,l}BG_{i,l}+K_{i,l}BK_{i,l}.$$ Both maps are unital and completely positive, and are contractions in operator norm, also after tensoring with the identity map on any auxiliary matrix algebra. The completely bounded norm, denoted by $\\|\\cdot\\|_{\\mathrm{cb}}$, is the supremum of the operator norms on all such auxiliary extensions. In this norm, $$\\|\\mathcal E_i-\\mathcal E_{i,l}\\|_{\\mathrm{cb}}\n          \\le Ce^{-cl^\\alpha}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-channel-tail}$$ The map $\\mathcal E_{i,l}$ fixes every operator commuting with the full algebra on $N_l(a_i)$, including operators supported outside that ball. All these conclusions allow arbitrary spectator auxiliary systems.",

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-truncation",
          "exact_quote": "Use Proposition <a href=\"#prop:positive\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:positive\">10</a> with $p=1$, so $\\alpha=1/2$. Fix $C_0>0$. There is a constant $C_1$, depending only on $q,R,J,\\Delta,C_0$, with the following property for every real $n\\ge2$ and every nonempty $S_0\\subseteq\\Lambda$ with $|S_0|\\le C_0n^2$. Put $r_0=\\lceil C_1(\\log n)^2\\rceil$. If $d_i^0:=d_\\Lambda(a_i,S_0)<\\infty$, define $$r_i=\\max\\{r_0,\\lfloor d_i^0/2\\rfloor\\},\\qquad\n \\widetilde h_i=k_{i,r_i},\\qquad \\widetilde X_i=N_{r_i}(a_i).\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-variable-radius}$$ If $d_i^0=\\infty$, set $\\widetilde h_i=k_i$ and designate its anchor’s entire component as $\\widetilde X_i$. Then $\\widetilde H=\\sum_i\\widetilde h_i$ is a sum of positive contractions and $$\\|\\widetilde H-H_F\\|\\le\\epsilon_n,\n \\qquad \\epsilon_n:=\\min\\{n^{-1000},g/4\\}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-truncation-error}$$ Its ground energy $\\widetilde E_0$ lies in $[0,\\epsilon_n]$, its ground vector $\\widetilde\\Omega$ is unique, and its gap is at least $g/2$. After a choice of phase, $$\\|\\widetilde\\Omega-\\Omega\\|\\le2\\sqrt{\\epsilon_n/g},\\qquad\n \\frac12\\big\\||\\widetilde\\Omega\\rangle\\langle\\widetilde\\Omega|\n                 -P_\\Omega\\big\\|_1\\le\\sqrt{2\\epsilon_n/g}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-ground-distance}$$*\n\n\n\n*For a set $X\\subseteq S_0$, let $b_X=|\\partial_\\Lambda X|$ and let $\\mathcal C_X$ be the labels whose designated supports $\\widetilde X_i$ meet both $X$ and $\\Lambda\\setminus X$. Every such support has radius exactly $r_0$, and $$|\\mathcal C_X|\\le Cb_X(r_0+1)^2,\\qquad\n \\log d_i\\le C(r_0+1)^2\\quad(i\\in\\mathcal C_X),\\qquad\n d_i:=q^{|\\widetilde X_i|}.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-crossing-count}$$ Consequently the cut parameter $$\\mathcal B_X:=1+\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal C_X}\\log^2(e d_i)\n       \\le C(1+b_X)(r_0+1)^6.\n \\label{eq:quasilocal-cut-budget}$$ In particular, $b_X\\le C_2nD$ and $D\\ge1$ imply $\\mathcal B_X\\le CnD(\\log n)^{12}$, with the constant also depending on $C_2$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-movement",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\theta$ be a unit pure vector on four finite-dimensional systems $P,x,U,F$, and let $\\rho_D$ denote its marginal on $D$. Set $$d=\\dim x,\\quad \\ell=\\log(ed),\\quad\n \\eta=S(x|P)_\\theta+S(x|U)_\\theta\n      =I(x:F|U)_\\theta=I(x:F|P)_\\theta.$$ There are universal constants $c,C>0$ such that, for $0<a\\ell\\le c$ and arbitrary density matrices $\\sigma$ on $xP$ and $\\tau$ on $xU$, $$\\label{eq:conditional-movement}\n \\left\\|\\sigma^{a/2}\\widehat\\rho_P^{-a/2}\n          \\tau^{a/2}\\widehat\\rho_U^{-a/2}\\theta\\right\\|\n \\le\\exp\\left(-\\frac a2\\eta+C a^{5/4}\\ell^2\\right).$$ The same bound holds for positive subnormalized $\\sigma,\\tau$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }

      "id": "step-conditional-movement",
      "inputs": [

      "method": "Conditional Schatten interpolation with retained Hölder slack and continuity.",
      "output": "A norm contraction governed by conditional information.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-lem-movement"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-lem-conditional-phases",
      "depends_on": [],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-conditional-phases",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\theta$ be a unit pure vector on finite-dimensional systems $P,x,U,F$, write $\\rho_D$ for its marginals, and put $d=\\dim x$ and $\\eta=I(x:F|U)_\\theta$. For $\\eta>0$ define $$y=\\min(1,\\eta),\\qquad\n \\mathcal R_\\eta=\\sqrt y+\\sqrt{\\eta\\log(ed/y)},$$ and set $\\mathcal R_0=0$. There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for every $u\\in\\mathbb R$, $$\\label{eq:conditional-modular-bound}\n \\big\\|\\big(\\widehat\\rho_U^{-iu}\\widehat\\rho_{xU}^{iu}\n       -\\widehat\\rho_{UF}^{-iu}\\widehat\\rho_{xUF}^{iu}\\big)\n                                            \\theta\\big\\|\n \\le C|\\sinh(\\pi u)|\\mathcal R_\\eta.$$ In particular the two phase products agree on $\\theta$ if $\\eta=0$. The constants do not depend on $\\dim P$, $\\dim U$, or $\\dim F$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-phase-comparison",
      "inputs": [
        "Conditional mutual information",

      "method": "Integrate a nonnegative resolvent defect and control the integral endpoints by dimension moments.",
      "output": "A dimension-controlled marginal-phase discrepancy.",

    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-lem-skew",

      ],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-skew",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\theta$ be a unit pure vector on $P,x,U,F$, put $Y=xU$, and write $\\rho_D$ for its marginals. Suppose $P=P_0P_1$ and that $0\\le h\\le I$ is supported on $P_0x$. Set $$d_h=(\\dim P_0)(\\dim x),\\qquad \\ell_h=\\log(ed_h),\\qquad\n \\eta=I(x:F|U)_\\theta=I(x:F|P)_\\theta.$$ Define the entire scalar function $$f(z)=\\langle\\theta,\n       \\rho_P^{[z]}\\rho_Y^{[-z]}h\n       \\rho_P^{[-z]}\\rho_Y^{[z]}\\theta\\rangle.$$ There are universal constants $c,C>0$ such that for $0<a\\ell_h\\le c$ and $t=a/2$, $$\\label{eq:conditional-skew}\n |f(t)|-\\Re f(t)\\le C a^2\\ell_h^4\\eta^{1/8}.$$ In particular the left side is zero if $\\eta=0$.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-local-skew",
      "inputs": [
        "Positive local contraction",
        "Marginal-phase discrepancy",
        "Support dimension"

      "method": "Combine phase comparison, narrow-strip bounds and Cauchy estimates.",
      "output": "Real-power scalar skew bounded by conditional information.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-lem-skew"
    },
    {
      "claim_anchor": "stmt-lem-schur",
      "depends_on": [],
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-schur",
          "exact_quote": "For the finite-dimensional tensor systems just defined, the following statements hold.*\n\n\n1.  *For $\\lambda\\vdash k$ of length at most $q$, put $l_i=\\lambda_i+q-i$ for $1\\le i\\le q$. Then $$\\label{replicas:dimensions}\n     \\dim V^{(q)}_\\lambda\n       =\\prod_{i<j}\\frac{l_i-l_j}{j-i},\\qquad\n     d_\\lambda=\\frac{k!\\prod_{i<j}(l_i-l_j)}{\\prod_i l_i!},\\qquad\n     \\log d_\\lambda=kH(\\lambda/k)+O_q(\\log(k+2)).$$ The number of labels and the sum of their general-linear multiplicities are polynomially bounded in $k$, with $q$ fixed.*\n\n2.  *Central label functions commute for nested or disjoint subsystems. On $\\mathcal S_k$, complementary label projectors agree: $\\pi_{Q,k}^{\\lambda}=\\pi_{Q^c,k}^{\\lambda}$.*\n\n\n\n3.  *If $Q,E$ are disjoint and their labels $\\lambda,\\mu$ are compatible with label $\\nu$ on $QE$, then $$\\label{replicas:merge-dimensions}\n     d_\\nu\\le d_\\lambda d_\\mu,\\qquad\n     d_\\lambda\\le d_\\nu d_\\mu.$$ For a tensor product of permutation-invariant density matrices on $Q^{\\otimes k}$ and $E^{\\otimes k}$, the conditional probability of $\\nu$ given $\\lambda,\\mu$ is at most $\\mathop{\\mathrm{poly}}(k)d_\\nu/(d_\\lambda d_\\mu)$. Consequently, for $0\\le b\\le1$, $$\\label{replicas:merge-moment}\n     \\mathbb E\\left(\\frac{d_\\lambda d_\\mu}{d_\\nu}\\right)^b\n     \\le\\mathop{\\mathrm{poly}}(k),$$ uniformly in those density matrices.*\n\n4.  *Split the copies into specified groups of sizes $k-r$ and $r$. If their labels $\\alpha,\\beta$ on a fixed subsystem are compatible with the full label $\\lambda$, then $$\\label{replicas:group-dimensions}\n     d_\\alpha d_\\beta\\le d_\\lambda\n           \\le \\binom{k}{r}d_\\alpha d_\\beta.$$ These subgroup label projectors commute with the full label projector.*\n\n\n5.  *If $\\rho$ is any permutation-invariant density matrix on $Q^{\\otimes k}$ and $L_\\rho=-\\log\\rho$ on its support, then $F_Q$ commutes with $\\rho$, $0\\le F_Q\\le L_\\rho$ on that support, and $$\\label{replicas:surprisal-moment}\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{Tr}}\\rho\\exp\\bigl(b(L_\\rho-F_Q)\\bigr)\\le\\mathop{\\mathrm{poly}}(k)\n           \\qquad(0\\le b\\le1).$$*\n\n\n6.  *The full $Q$ label $\\lambda$ and the first-$(k-1)$ label $\\nu$ are compatible precisely along the possible removable-row branches $\\nu=\\lambda-e_i$. In any permutation-invariant $Q$ state, conditional on $\\lambda$, the probability of this branch is $$\\label{replicas:branch-probability}\n     p_{\\lambda,i}=\\frac{d_{\\lambda-e_i}}{d_\\lambda}\n     =\\frac{l_i}{k}\\frac{\\prod_{a<b}(l_a-\\delta_{ai}-l_b+\\delta_{bi})}\n                             {\\prod_{a<b}(l_a-l_b)}\n     \\le 2^q\\frac{l_i}{k}.$$ The normalized Jucys–Murphy, or star, operator (Vershik and Okounkov 2005, sec. 2) [[VershikOkounkov2005](#ref-VershikOkounkov2005)] $$\\label{replicas:star-definition}\n     J_{Q,k}=\\frac1k\\sum_{j<k}U_Q((j\\ k))$$ has eigenvalue $(\\lambda_i-i)/k$ on that branch.*\n\n*The polynomial bounds may depend on the fixed subsystem dimensions, but not on the density matrices.",
          "source_id": "PM-265.1"
        }

          "exact_quote": "The operators in <a href=\"#replicas:w-definition\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"replicas:w-definition\">[replicas:w-definition]</a> are positive definite and central. Uniformly in their labels, $$\\label{replicas:W-comparison}\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{poly}}(k)^{-1}e^{-tF_{Q,k}}\\le W_{Q,k}\n       \\le\\mathop{\\mathrm{poly}}(k)e^{-tF_{Q,k}}.$$ On $\\mathcal S_k$, $W_{Q,k}=W_{Q^c,k}$ exactly. For each subsystem there is a probability measure on positive definite subdensities $\\sigma$ on $Q$, with $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Tr}}\\sigma\\le1$, such that $$\\label{replicas:W-integral}\n W_{Q,k}=\\int(\\sigma^t)^{\\otimes k}\\,d\\zeta_Q(\\sigma)\n                  \\qquad(k\\ge0).$$ The measure is independent of $k$.*\n\n\n\n*Extend $W_{Q,k-1}$ by the identity on the last copy and define $R_{Q,k}=W_{Q,k}W_{Q,k-1}^{-1}$. Then $$\\label{replicas:R-forward}\n \\lVert R_{Q,k}-(J_{Q,k})_+^t\\rVert\\longrightarrow0$$ on the entire tensor space. There is a constant $C_{\\mathcal V,t}$ such that, for every unit $z\\in\\mathcal S_k$, $\\lVert R_{Q,k}^{-1}z\\rVert\\le C_{\\mathcal V,t}$, and $$\\label{replicas:R-inverse}\n \\limsup_{k\\to\\infty}\\sup_{\\substack{z\\in\\mathcal S_k\\\\\\lVert z\\rVert=1}}\n \\lVert \\bigl(R_{Q,k}^{-1}-\\max(J_{Q,k},\\delta)^{-t}\\bigr)z\\rVert\n \\le C_{\\mathcal V,t}\\delta^{(1-2t)/2}\n                 \\qquad(0<\\delta<1).$$",

          "anchor": "stmt-transport-means",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal T$ be a weighted binary tree with terminal weights $w_j$ and positive definite inputs $A_j$, and let $M$ be its root. Then $M=\\prod_{g=1}^K M_g$, where $M_g$ is the root of the same weighted tree with inputs $A_{j,g}$. The factors $M_g$ commute.",

        }

          "exact_quote": "For real $z$, $$\\label{transport:g-fourier}\n g_s(z)=\\int_{\\mathbb R}e^{iuz}m_s(u)\\,du,\n \\qquad m_s(u)>0,\\qquad \\int_{\\mathbb R}m_s(u)\\,du=2s.$$ For $s=1/4$, the functions $$\\label{transport:h-def}\n h_\\pm(z)=\\frac{e^{\\pm sz}-1}{2\\sinh(z/2)}\n =\\pm e^{\\pm sz/2}g_{s/2}(z)$$ have Fourier densities $$\\label{transport:q-density}\n q_\\pm(u)=\\pm m_{s/2}(u\\pm is/2),\\qquad\n |q_\\pm(u)|\\leq\\frac1{\\sqrt2}m_s(u).$$ The quotients in <a href=\"#transport:h-def\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"transport:h-def\">[transport:h-def]</a> are interpreted continuously at zero.",

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-transport",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a finite one-copy space, history and conditional choice trees, partitions, cross-band commutation, positive parameter $a$, and positive contractions with designated supports as specified above.           "anchor": "stmt-prop-comparators",
          "exact_quote": "Fix the positive gapped Hamiltonian and physical target $X$ above, a finite collection of status partitions satisfying <a href=\"#comparator:nesting\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:nesting\">[comparator:nesting]</a>, a typical Schmidt set satisfying <a href=\"#comparator:typical-set\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:typical-set\">[comparator:typical-set]</a>, and a mean tree with metrics <a href=\"#comparator:metrics\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:metrics\">[comparator:metrics]</a>. There is a sequence of common auxiliary labels $\\lambda_k$ and nonzero vectors $$\\mathrm{pre}_k=\\pi_R^{\\lambda_k}\n  (\\widetilde\\Omega\\otimes\\mathrm{Bell}_{CR})^{\\otimes k}\n       \\in\\mathcal S_k,\n \\qquad \\|\\mathrm{pre}_k\\|\\le1,\n \\label{comparator:prevector}$$ Here $\\pi_R^{\\lambda_k}$ is the Schur-label projection on the $R$ copies. These vectors are physical mean-energy eigenvectors of eigenvalue $\\widetilde E_0$ and have label $\\lambda_k$ on both $C$ and $R$. For every tree above, set $$N=\\|\\mathcal M^{-s}\\mathrm{pre}_k\\|,\n \\qquad v=\\mathcal M^{-s}\\mathrm{pre}_k/N,\n \\qquad\n E_{\\mathrm{def}}=\n \\frac{\\langle v,\\overline{\\widetilde H}v\\rangle-\\widetilde E_0}\n      {\\widetilde g},\n \\qquad\n \\overline{\\widetilde H}=\\frac1k\\sum_{i=1}^k\\widetilde H^{(i)}.$$ *Rough comparisons.* For $0<\\tau<1/2$, the upper bound below uses the prefix data <a href=\"#comparator:prefix-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:prefix-data\">[comparator:prefix-data]</a>: $$\\begin{aligned}\n -\\frac{\\log N^2}{k}\n &\\le 2\\log d_*-\\log z+\n       2sW\\left(\\frac{2B_{\\mathrm{sh}}}{z}+2B_{\\mathrm{exc}}\\right)\n       +o_k(1),\n \\label{comparator:rough-upper}\\\\\n -\\frac{\\log N^2}{k}\n &\\ge 2sW\\left[\n       2S'-C\\left(\\tau\\log d_*+\\frac{h(\\tau)}a\\right)\n       -C\\frac{E_{\\mathrm{def}}}{\\tau}S'\\right]-o_k(1).\n \\label{comparator:rough-lower}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $h$ is binary entropy. The lower bound does not require <a href=\"#comparator:prefix-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:prefix-data\">[comparator:prefix-data]</a> or <a href=\"#comparator:mgf-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:mgf-data\">[comparator:mgf-data]</a>.*\n\n\n\n\n**Sharp comparisons.* If <a href=\"#comparator:mgf-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:mgf-data\">[comparator:mgf-data]</a> holds and $a\\le c/\\sqrt{\\mathcal B}$, with $c$ sufficiently small in terms of $c_0$, define $$\\begin{aligned}\n g_{j,g}^{\\mathrm{pre}}\n   &=S(XU_{j,g})+S(V_{j,g})-S(Y_{j,g}),\\\\\n g_{j,g}^{\\mathrm{post}}\n   &=S(U_{j,g})+S(U_{j,g}Y_{j,g})-S(Y_{j,g}),\n \\qquad g_{\\max}=\\max_{j,g}g_{j,g}^{\\mathrm{pre}}.\n\\end{aligned}$$ Then $g_{j,g}^{\\mathrm{pre}}\\ge0$, and the sharp comparisons are $$\\begin{aligned}\n -\\frac{\\log N^2}{k}\n &\\le 2\\log d_*-\\log z+\n  2sW\\left[\\langle g^{\\mathrm{post}}\\rangle_{\\mathrm{av}}\n          +C\\left(a\\mathcal B+\\frac{|\\log z|}{a}\\right)\\right]\n          +o_k(1),\n \\label{comparator:sharp-upper}\\\\\n -\\frac{\\log N^2}{k}\n &\\ge 2sW\\left[2S'+(1-\\tau)\n                  \\langle g^{\\mathrm{pre}}\\rangle_{\\mathrm{av}}\n       -C\\left(\\tau\\log d_*+\\frac{h(\\tau)}a+a\\mathcal B\\right)\n       -C\\frac{E_{\\mathrm{def}}}{\\tau}(S'+g_{\\max})\\right]\n       -o_k(1).\n \\label{comparator:sharp-lower}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The upper sharp bound does not require <a href=\"#comparator:prefix-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"comparator:prefix-data\">[comparator:prefix-data]</a>. For every physical partition there is the exact identity $$2S_X+g_{j,g}^{\\mathrm{pre}}-g_{j,g}^{\\mathrm{post}}\n       =I(X:V_{j,g})+I(X:Y_{j,g}V_{j,g}).\n \\label{comparator:entropy-identity}$$*\n\n*All replica limits are taken with the physical system, auxiliary dimensions, finite status collection and tree, $a$, and $\\tau$ fixed. The errors are uniform over terminal probabilities, including their dependence on $k$, and over the symmetric vectors to which the lower comparison is applied. Constants or degrees in intermediate polynomial factors in $k$ may depend on the fixed entire system. They disappear in $o_k(1)$. The displayed constants in the rough bounds are universal; those in the sharp bounds may also depend on $C_0,c_0$. None has additional dependence on the system dimensions.",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-scanner-histories",
          "exact_quote": "Under <a href=\"#scanner:scales\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"scanner:scales\">[scanner:scales]</a>–<a href=\"#scanner:test-geometry\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"scanner:test-geometry\">[scanner:test-geometry]</a>, the preceding construction has the following properties for all sufficiently large $n$.*\n\n1.  *Every splitting designated support is a graph $r_0$-ball wholly inside $A$. It splits at most one band, and there it meets $Y$ and exactly one of the two sides. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-uniform-area-bound**: The ground-state entropy of every region is bounded by its crossing-edge count with a constant depending only on the fixed Hamiltonian parameters and global gap. Domain size, shape, holes, and disconnectedness do not change that constant.
- **invariant-positive-gap-domination**: The exact positive constraints annihilate the original ground vector separately, retain a global gap through operator domination, and have spatial tails controlled in graph distance.
- **invariant-common-transport-states**: Entropy gain and excitation-energy cost are controlled through the same transported density matrices. The energy estimate contains both the individual term's split probability and the weighted sum over its split leaves.
- **invariant-fixed-instance-replica-limit**: The physical system, auxiliary dimensions, partitions, exponents, and finite schedule are fixed before the replica limit. Uniformity over replica density matrices permits states and interpolation choices to depend on the copy count without changing this order.
- **invariant-amplified-remote-decoupling**: A sublinear collar information bound, together with the stated size and boundary budgets, yields arbitrarily strong inverse-power mutual-information bounds outside an enlarged graph neighborhood. The conclusion also holds after discarding part of the target.
- **invariant-two-family-cancellation**: For a pure state, mutual-information control against the complement and all preceding regions in each ordered family cancels the individual region entropies. The remaining entropy cost comes from the exceptional set and the summed information errors.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-gapless-or-degenerate-ground-space**: Apply the area bound to a gapless Hamiltonian or to an arbitrary vector in a degenerate ground space. -> The uniform entropy conclusion is not established when the unique-ground-vector and positive global-gap assumptions fail.
- **anti-use-ambient-distance-for-locality**: Replace induced-graph distance by ambient distance when truncating interactions or propagating operators around holes. -> Ambient proximity does not supply a path inside the physical domain, and separate components must remain uncoupled.
- **anti-use-efficient-peps-construction**: Treat the entropy theorem and its stated tensor-network consequence as an efficient procedure for producing or contracting a ground-state representation. -> The existence statement supplies no efficient tensor construction or contraction algorithm. The companion representation conclusion uses additional arguments beyond the entropy inequality.
- **anti-use-exchanging-replica-and-volume-limits**: Increase the physical volume or auxiliary dimensions together with the replica count and reuse the fixed-instance remainder estimates. -> Polynomial degrees and convergence rates may depend on the entire fixed finite instance. Uniformity over replica states does not imply uniformity over growing physical systems.
- **anti-use-truncations-as-exact-annihilators**: Assume that conditional expectation preserves exact ground-state annihilation and insert the scanner's truncated constraints into the amplification argument. -> The truncated constraints can perturb the ground vector. Amplification instead uses a fresh exact positive system, so its large restoring-operator norm does not amplify a scanner truncation error.
- **anti-use-single-split-weight**: Replace the coupled entropy-energy transport estimate with a generic bound charging only one split-probability factor. -> The scanner's low-energy estimate relies on the additional split weight obtained by transporting the square and applying Cauchy–Schwarz. A weakened bound does not justify the same scale comparison.
- **anti-use-birth-to-birth-separation**: Require disjoint birth templates for every ancestor and descendant, or justify ordered clearance by shrinking only the newly created region. -> An ancestor's original birth region can overlap a replacement. The needed clearance compares the new entire birth template with the older final actual region after removal.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The principal result is a uniform analytic entropy inequality over arbitrary admissible finite domains, rather than a finite input-output construction with an executable correctness oracle. Its proof uses optimized operators, spectral integrals, and symmetric-replica limits. The source explicitly states: “Every limit below is taken with $\mathcal V$, its factorization, and all real exponents fixed.” It further states: “A cutoff and a polynomial approximation are fixed before taking $k\to\infty$; their errors are removed only afterwards.” Finite enumeration of selected Hamiltonians or geometric examples would not decide these limits or certify the uniform area-law constant. The stated tensor-network consequence also says: “This is an existence result; it does not assert an efficient tensor construction or contraction algorithm.”

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-unique-global-ground-state** (hypothesis): The area law requires a unique normalized ground vector and a positive gap for the full Hamiltonian. It supplies no conclusion for an arbitrary vector in a degenerate ground space or for a gapless model. Blocked use: ['Apply the uniform entropy bound without establishing ground-state uniqueness and the full-system gap.']
- **limit-fixed-local-parameters** (hypothesis): Local dimension, induced-graph interaction range and interaction strength must remain within the fixed admissible bounds. The entropy constant cannot be treated as uniform when these parameters or the gap lower bound vary outside that regime. Blocked use: ['Transfer the same entropy constant to unbounded local dimensions, unbounded interaction strengths or unrestricted long-range interactions.']
- **limit-induced-square-lattice-geometry** (formal_scope): The theorem covers finite induced square-lattice domains. Holes and disconnected components are allowed, but arbitrary interaction graphs and other lattice geometries are outside the asserted conclusion. Blocked use: ['Infer the same area law for arbitrary graphs or higher-dimensional lattices from the geometric decomposition.']
- **limit-graph-versus-ambient-distance** (formal_scope): Operator locality and propagation use paths in the induced graph. Ambient clearance supplies a sufficient separation condition but does not establish the existence of an ambiently short physical path. Blocked use: ['Replace graph neighborhoods by ambient neighborhoods when assigning interaction range or propagation distances around holes.']
- **limit-empty-boundary-and-product-cases** (edge_case): Cuts without crossing edges require the component-factorization argument. Empty domains, trivial local spaces and on-site-only interactions are separately covered by vanishing entropy or product-state arguments. Blocked use: ['Require a positive boundary budget in cases handled by factorization or the trivial-system conventions.']
- **limit-controlled-continuity-dimension** (hypothesis): Continuity costs depend on the controlled first system's dimension. Independence from spectator dimension does not remove dependence on the target dimension. Blocked use: ['Use spectator-independent continuity to claim a dimension-free entropy error for a growing controlled subsystem.']
- **limit-surprisal-center-not-bounded** (formal_scope): The marginal-tail estimate controls fluctuations around the entropy. It does not by itself bound the entropy center or prove the area law. Blocked use: ['Deduce a boundary-proportional entropy bound solely from concentration of marginal surprisal.']
- **limit-safe-buffer-and-filter-optimization** (nonconstructive): The initial entropy discount requires a safe parent and containment of the padded rectangle. Its proof maximizes over compact matrix feasible sets and subsequently removes the positivity floor; it provides no stated solver or runtime guarantee. Blocked use: ['Apply the buffer discount near the cut without its safety and padding conditions.', 'Treat stationarity of the optimizing filters as a convergent computational procedure.']
- **limit-truncated-annihilation** (approximation): Conditional expectation preserves positivity but may destroy exact ground-state annihilation. The truncated Hamiltonian must be used with its own exact ground vector and the stated perturbation and gap margins. Blocked use: ['Treat spatially truncated constraints as exact annihilators of the original ground vector.', 'Ignore the testing-set size condition or the gap cap on the perturbation.']
- **limit-conditional-powers-and-smallness** (hypothesis): The movement and skew estimates require pure finite-dimensional partitioned states, their specified support-power conventions and dimension-dependent smallness conditions. The skew estimate additionally requires a local positive contraction. Blocked use: ['Use ordinary inverses on marginal kernels.', 'Apply the skew bound to an unrestricted operator or outside the stated power-parameter regime.']
- **limit-fixed-instance-replica-order** (formal_scope): Replica limits hold after fixing the entire finite one-copy system, factorization and exponents. Clipping and polynomial approximation errors are removed afterwards. Uniformity over replica states does not justify simultaneous growth of physical or auxiliary dimensions. Blocked use: ['Exchange the physical-volume limit with the replica limit.', 'Treat finite replica agreement as certification of the limiting symbol calculus.']
- **limit-tree-and-common-state-transport** (hypothesis): Transport requires the specified finite trees, cross-band commutation, support-splitting geometry and power smallness. Its energy conclusion also requires the prevector eigenvector assumption. The tree structure and both split-weight factors are part of the argument. Blocked use: ['Reassociate operator means without justification.', 'Use unrelated states for entropy gain and energy cost.', "Discard the additional split probability while retaining the scanner's claimed energy scaling."]
- **limit-comparator-regime-distinction** (hypothesis): Norm comparisons require nested status partitions and a typical Schmidt set. The rough upper comparison uses prefix entropy and mismatch data, while the sharp comparisons additionally require marginal moment bounds and their power-parameter restriction. Blocked use: ['Invoke sharp norm comparisons using only the rough prefix assumptions.', 'Apply the auxiliary-pair comparisons to arbitrary nonnested partitions.']
- **limit-scanner-selection-and-template-clearance** (hypothesis): The scanner requires its scale ordering, controlled depth rows, cut clearance, entropy inputs and sufficiently large scale. Averaging selects an interpolation point that may depend on the replica count. The collar result applies to the specified separated templates with the prescribed collar contained within the piece scale. Blocked use: ['Apply the collar bound to unrestricted target shapes or insufficiently separated targets.', 'Replace existence of a selected low-energy interpolation by a guarantee for every round and parameter.']
- **limit-exact-product-amplification-and-remoteness** (hypothesis): Amplification uses fresh exact positive constraints, a sublinear information input and controlled size and crossing-edge budgets. Its conclusion applies simultaneously to remote sets outside the enlarged graph neighborhood, at sufficiently large scale with constants allowed to depend on the requested inverse-power accuracy. Blocked use: ["Reuse the scanner's truncated constraints as the exact amplification system.", 'Claim decoupling for physical sets inside the enlarged neighborhood.', 'Include the cut complement without establishing the additional clearance condition.']
- **limit-ordered-birth-to-actual-clearance** (formal_scope): The geometric argument compares an entire new birth template with earlier final actual regions of the same family. Ancestor birth regions need not be disjoint from replacement birth regions. Entropy cancellation requires disjoint physical regions, separate family orders and purity. Blocked use: ['Substitute birth-to-birth separation for the asserted ordered clearance.', 'Shrink only the new region when the proof requires removal from old identifiers.', 'Apply the cancellation inequality to a mixed state without another argument.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove an entropy area law for the unique ground state of a finite-range Hamiltonian on any finite induced subgraph of the square lattice. A lower bound on the spectral gap of the full Hamiltonian and fixed bounds on the local dimension, interaction range, and interaction strength suffice. For every set of sites, its entanglement entropy is bounded by a constant times the number of edges crossing its boundary, independently of the size and shape of the domain.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

The entanglement entropy of a pure quantum state measures how much information is shared by a region and its complement. Its elementary upper bound is proportional to the number of sites in the region. An area law replaces this volume by the number of interactions crossing the region’s boundary. We prove such a bound for the unique gapped ground state of a general finite-range Hamiltonian in two dimensions.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The setting and the theorem

<a id="eq:hamiltonian"></a>
Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^2$ be finite. Its edges join pairs at Euclidean distance one, so that $\Lambda$ carries the induced square-lattice graph. Write $d_\Lambda$ for graph distance, with value $+\infty$ between different components. At each site put a copy of $\mathbb C^q$, and write $\mathcal H_\Lambda=\bigotimes_{x\in\Lambda}\mathbb C^q$. An operator supported on $X\subseteq\Lambda$ acts as the identity on the other tensor factors. An admissible Hamiltonian has the form $$\label{eq:hamiltonian}
 H=\sum_{\substack{\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\Lambda\\
                  \mathop{\mathrm{diam}}_{d_\Lambda}X\le R}}h_X,
 \qquad h_X=h_X^*,\qquad \lVert h_X\rVert\le J.$$ There is one summand for each support $X$; a summand may be zero. Here $q\ge1$ and $R\ge0$ are fixed integers and $J>0$ is fixed. This indexing convention bounds the sum of interaction norms at every site in terms of $R,J$ alone.

For $A\subseteq\Lambda$ define the edge boundary $$\partial_\Lambda A=
 \{\{x,y\}:x\in A,\ y\in\Lambda\setminus A,\ |x-y|_1=1\}.$$ If $\Omega\in\mathcal H_\Lambda$ is a unit vector, write $\rho_A=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\Lambda\setminus A}\lvert \Omega\rangle\langle \Omega\rvert$ and $S_\Omega(A)=-\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}\rho_A\log\rho_A$, with $0\log0=0$. All logarithms are natural.

<a id="stmt-thm-area"></a>
<div id="thm:area" class="theorem">

<a id="eq:area-law"></a>
**Theorem 1** (Area law). *For every $q,R,J$ as above and every $\Delta>0$, there is a finite constant $C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ with the following property. Suppose that $\Lambda$ is a finite induced square-lattice domain and that the Hamiltonian <a href="#eq:hamiltonian" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hamiltonian">[eq:hamiltonian]</a> has a unique normalized ground vector $\Omega$, up to phase, with ground energy $E_0$, and satisfies $$H-E_0\mathop{\mathrm{id}}\ \ge\ \Delta\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{id}}-\lvert \Omega\rangle\langle \Omega\rvert\bigr).$$ Then for every $A\subseteq\Lambda$, $$\label{eq:area-law}
 S_\Omega(A)\le C\,|\partial_\Lambda A|.$$ The same constant applies to all such domains, sets, and Hamiltonians.*

</div>

The distance in <a href="#eq:hamiltonian" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hamiltonian">[eq:hamiltonian]</a> is the distance within the induced graph. This distinction matters for domains with holes or disconnected components. The spectral assumption concerns the full Hamiltonian; no gap assumption is imposed on Hamiltonians restricted to smaller regions.

For completeness, the theorem also gives the usual vertex-boundary formulations. Define $$\partial_{\rm in}A=\{x\in A:\exists y\notin A,
                \ \{x,y\}\in\partial_\Lambda A\},
 \qquad
 Z_A=\bigcup_{e\in\partial_\Lambda A}e.$$

<a id="stmt-cor-rectangles"></a>
<div id="cor:rectangles" class="corollary">

**Corollary 2**. *The conclusion of Theorem <a href="#thm:area" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:area">1</a> holds for every subset of a finite rectangular square lattice with bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions and a unique ground state separated by a fixed global gap. For every domain covered by that theorem it also implies $$S_\Omega(A)\le4C|\partial_{\rm in}A|,
 \qquad S_\Omega(A)\le2C|Z_A|.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-cor-rectangles"><summary>Proof of stmt-cor-rectangles</summary>

*Proof.* On-site and nearest-neighbor interactions have graph range at most one. Each inner boundary vertex is incident with between one and four crossing edges, so $|\partial_{\rm in}A|\le|\partial_\Lambda A|
\le4|\partial_{\rm in}A|$. Counting both endpoints gives $|Z_A|\le2|\partial_\Lambda A|\le4|Z_A|$. These inequalities include empty boundaries. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### History and related work

The relation between entanglement and boundary area arose in quantum-field calculations motivated by black-hole entropy. Bombelli, Koul, Lee, and Sorkin related entropy from tracing inaccessible quantum-field degrees of freedom to black-hole area (Bombelli et al. 1986) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[BombelliEtAl1986](#ref-BombelliEtAl1986)]; Srednicki subsequently found area scaling numerically for a spherical region in the vacuum of a regulated free massless scalar field (Srednicki 1993) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Srednicki1993](#ref-Srednicki1993)]. These calculations motivated the entanglement area-law question through regulated field models. For finite-dimensional lattice spins, the gap-to-area conjecture asks whether a unique ground state has an entropy bound proportional to boundary area when local dimension, interaction range and strength are bounded and the spectral gap has a size-independent positive lower bound (Hastings 2007; Arad, Landau, and Vazirani 2012) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Hastings2007](#ref-Hastings2007), [AradLandauVazirani2012](#ref-AradLandauVazirani2012)]. Theorem <a href="#thm:area" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:area">1</a> gives an affirmative answer in the stated two-dimensional induced-domain setting.

In one dimension, Hastings proved a length-independent entropy bound for the unique ground state of a finite-range Hamiltonian with uniformly bounded interactions, fixed local dimension, and a positive spectral gap (Hastings 2007) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Hastings2007](#ref-Hastings2007)]. Arad, Landau, and Vazirani improved the dependence on the inverse gap for frustration-free chains using approximate ground-state projectors (Arad, Landau, and Vazirani 2012) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[AradLandauVazirani2012](#ref-AradLandauVazirani2012)]. These are operators that preserve the ground vector while contracting its orthogonal complement, with controlled growth of Schmidt rank. Arad, Kitaev, Landau, and Vazirani extended this approach to general, possibly frustrated chains (Arad et al. 2013) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[AradKitaevLandauVazirani2013](#ref-AradKitaevLandauVazirani2013)]. A complementary result of Brandão and Horodecki derives an area law for pure one-dimensional states from exponential decay of correlations between arbitrary separated regions (Brandão and Horodecki 2015) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[BrandaoHorodecki2015](#ref-BrandaoHorodecki2015)]. This region-wise hypothesis is stronger than decay of single-site correlation functions. More generally, the exponential clustering theorem relates a spectral gap to decay of connected correlations of separated observables (Nachtergaele and Sims 2006) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[NachtergaeleSims2006](#ref-NachtergaeleSims2006)]; an entropy estimate requires control of the reduced state’s full spectrum. Anshu, Harrow, and Soleimanifar obtained boundary-dependent bounds on smooth entanglement spread, which measures the width of the significant part of that spectrum, including square-root boundary scaling on lattices up to logarithmic factors (Anshu, Harrow, and Soleimanifar 2022) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[AnshuHarrowSoleimanifar2022](#ref-AnshuHarrowSoleimanifar2022)]. Such a width estimate leaves the location of the spectrum, and hence its entropy, to be controlled.

Strict area-law bounds in higher dimensions are also known for restricted model classes. Cramer, Eisert, Plenio, and Dreißig proved such a bound for arbitrary regions in cubic harmonic lattices with a finite-range positive potential matrix whose condition number is uniformly bounded (Cramer et al. 2006) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[CramerEisertPlenioDreissig2006](#ref-CramerEisertPlenioDreissig2006)]. These Gaussian models have infinite-dimensional oscillator sites and provide a comparison with the finite-dimensional spin setting considered here.

Other higher-dimensional results make additional spectral or thermodynamic assumptions. Masanes obtained bounds with logarithmic corrections from correlation decay and bounds on the number of low-energy states of restricted Hamiltonians (Masanes 2009) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Masanes2009](#ref-Masanes2009)]; Brandão and Cramer obtained a logarithmically corrected bound for cubic regions under a low-temperature heat-capacity hypothesis (Brandão and Cramer 2015) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[BrandaoCramer2015](#ref-BrandaoCramer2015)]. Cho proved strict area scaling for balls along boundary-growth families satisfying uniform gaps and an additional compatibility condition on successive reduced ground states (Cho 2014) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Cho2014](#ref-Cho2014)]. These conditions supply information beyond the gap of the single full Hamiltonian considered here.

For two-dimensional spin systems, Anshu, Arad, and Gosset proved a subvolume bound for rectangular regions in a rectangular lattice with plaquette projector interactions, a unique frustration-free ground state, and a uniform local gap (Anshu, Arad, and Gosset 2022b) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[AnshuAradGosset2022Subvolume](#ref-AnshuAradGosset2022Subvolume)]. At fixed local dimension and local gap, the bound is $O(b^{5/3}\log^{7/3}(2+b))$, where $b$ is the rectangle’s boundary size. Their subsequent result gives $$S\le n^{\,1+O((\log n)^{-1/5})}$$ across a vertical cut of length $n$, again for locally gapped, frustration-free plaquette projector models with a unique ground state (Anshu, Arad, and Gosset 2022a) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[AnshuAradGosset2022Area](#ref-AnshuAradGosset2022Area)]. The local-gap assumption concerns restrictions of the Hamiltonian; it is stronger than a gap for the full system alone. The latter entropy bound is near-linear, and its theorem concerns vertical cuts. The setting considered here allows frustrated interactions, assumes a gap only for the full Hamiltonian, and includes arbitrary regions in arbitrary finite induced square-lattice domains. Arad, Firanko, and Jain extend approximate-projector methods to maximally mixed ground states and bound their mutual information, with a two-dimensional application under frustration-free and local-gap assumptions (Arad, Firanko, and Jain 2026) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[AradFirankoJain2026](#ref-AradFirankoJain2026)].

The proof below combines locality estimates with ways of expressing entropy through operator norms. For locality, we use the Lieb–Robinson framework (Lieb and Robinson 1972; Nachtergaele, Ogata, and Sims 2006) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[LiebRobinson1972](#ref-LiebRobinson1972), [NachtergaeleOgataSims2006](#ref-NachtergaeleOgataSims2006)] and Kitaev’s centered spectral filter (Kitaev 2006, Appendix D.1.2) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[Kitaev2006Anyons](#ref-Kitaev2006Anyons)]. Swingle and McGreevy discuss positive constraints obtained by squaring filtered terms, for which retaining a gap is a separate issue (Swingle and McGreevy 2016, sec. 8.4) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[SwingleMcGreevy2016](#ref-SwingleMcGreevy2016)]. Here taking absolute values gives the operator domination that retains the full-system gap. Later, products of positive contractions derived from these constraints preserve the ground state and suppress excitations, as projection products do in detectability-lemma arguments (Anshu, Arad, and Vidick 2016) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[AnshuAradVidick2016](#ref-AnshuAradVidick2016)]. Their localization uses propagation estimates for unital channels, related to dissipative Lieb–Robinson bounds (Barthel and Kliesch 2012) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[BarthelKliesch2012](#ref-BarthelKliesch2012)]; the coupled random-product estimate needed here is proved in Section <a href="#sec:amplification" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:amplification">10</a>.

For the entropy comparison, bounds on local entanglement production are a precedent for controlling logarithmic commutators independently of spectator dimensions (Van Acoleyen, Mariën, and Verstraete 2013) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[VanAcoleyenMarienVerstraete2013](#ref-VanAcoleyenMarienVerstraete2013)]. Section <a href="#sec:initial" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:initial">3</a> proves the quadratic real-part estimate needed for our marginal tails. Strong subadditivity and conditional-entropy continuity supply the entropy inequalities used throughout (Lieb and Ruskai 1973; Alicki and Fannes 2004; Winter 2016) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[LiebRuskai1973](#ref-LiebRuskai1973), [AlickiFannes2004](#ref-AlickiFannes2004), [Winter2016](#ref-Winter2016)]. We encode marginal spectra on symmetric tensor powers using Schur–Weyl duality (Etingof et al. 2011) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[EtingofEtAl2011](#ref-EtingofEtAl2011)], whose connection with spectrum estimation is developed by Keyl and Werner (Keyl and Werner 2001) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[KeylWerner2001](#ref-KeylWerner2001)]. The passage back to one-copy vectors uses finite quantum de Finetti measures (Christandl et al. 2007; Lewin, Nam, and Rougerie 2015) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[ChristandlEtAl2007](#ref-ChristandlEtAl2007), [LewinNamRougerie2015](#ref-LewinNamRougerie2015)] and the product calculus of symmetrized finite observables (Raggio and Werner 1989) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[RaggioWerner1989](#ref-RaggioWerner1989)]. Weighted operator geometric means (Pusz and Woronowicz 1975; Kubo and Ando 1980) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[PuszWoronowicz1975](#ref-PuszWoronowicz1975), [KuboAndo1980](#ref-KuboAndo1980)] combine the changing partitions, while the modular comparison starts from the resolvent-compression identity of Carlen and Vershynina (Carlen and Vershynina 2020, Lemma 2.1) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[CarlenVershynina2019](#ref-CarlenVershynina2019)]. The detailed construction uses these ingredients to compare entropy gain and excitation energy in the same family of states; the next overview explains how that comparison leads to the area bound.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### A tensor-network consequence

A projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) is specified by one tensor at each lattice site, with a physical index for that site’s state and one virtual index for each incident edge. Contracting the paired virtual indices gives a many-body vector. The dimension of an edge index is its bond dimension. The approximation problem asks how large these dimensions must be to approximate the ground vector on the original lattice.

The companion (OpenAI 2026, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[OpenAI2026PolynomialPEPS](#ref-OpenAI2026PolynomialPEPS)] proves a polynomial bound for the original open $L\times L$ square grid, $L\ge2$, with on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions. For fixed local dimension $q\ge2$, term-norm bound $J>0$, and global gap $\Delta>0$, every unique ground vector in this class has a PEPS approximation with maximum bond dimension at most $CL^c$ and global vector error at most $L^{-1}$ after normalization and phase choice. The constants depend only on $q,J,\Delta$. This is an existence result; it does not assert an efficient tensor construction or contraction algorithm.

The approximation uses more than the entropy inequality. This paper also provides positive operators that annihilate the ground vector and have rapidly decaying spatial tails (Proposition <a href="#prop:positive" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:positive">10</a>), quantitative information bounds across collars (Propositions <a href="#prop:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:collar">30</a> and <a href="#prop:amplification" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:amplification">32</a>), and two families of geometrically separated regions (Proposition <a href="#prop:two-families" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:two-families">34</a>), with the region shapes and clearances specified in those results. The companion combines these estimates and the geometric ordering with additional compression and routing arguments; its PEPS result is a consequence of that further analysis.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### How the proof is organized

Fix the set $A$ whose entropy is to be bounded, and let $Z_A$ be its crossing-edge endpoints. For disjoint physical regions $B,C$, write $$I_\Omega(B:C)=S_\Omega(B)+S_\Omega(C)-S_\Omega(B\cup C)$$ for their mutual information. Our analytic goal is to make this quantity small when $B$ lies inside $A$ and $C$ is beyond a suitable collar, even when $C$ includes all of $\Lambda\setminus A$. Here is why this suffices. Suppose that, after removing a set $D$ of $O(|\partial_\Lambda A|)$ sites, we can partition $A$ into two ordered families of regions. If each region shares little information with the complement of $A$ together with the earlier regions of its own family, two applications of the entropy chain rule cancel all individual region entropies. Purity then bounds $S_\Omega(A)$ by $|D|\log q$ and the sum of the information errors. Section <a href="#sec:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:geometry">11</a> constructs regions with the required ordering and separation.

The analytic estimates concern intersections of $A$ with ambient boxes or finite unions of rectangles and triangles. Their clearance is from $Z_A$; they may meet holes or the edge of the physical domain. Hamiltonian locality and propagation always use neighborhoods in the induced graph. The argument has five stages.

1.  *Obtain a first exponent below volume.* Section <a href="#sec:initial" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:initial">3</a> uses the global gap to bound fluctuations of the negative logarithms of positive marginal eigenvalues. It then optimizes products of positive operators on nested rectangles. Two bounds on the optimized norm, one using the energy estimate and global gap, give a conditional-entropy discount, and hence $$S_\Omega(A\cap Q)\le Cr^{1+e_0},\qquad e_0<1,$$ for a box $Q$ of side at most $r$ sufficiently far from $Z_A$.

2.  *Control information and energy in the same interpolation.* Section <a href="#sec:quasilocal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:quasilocal">4</a> replaces the Hamiltonian by a sum of positive operators that annihilate $\Omega$ separately, retain a global gap, and have rapidly decaying graph-local tails. Sections <a href="#sec:conditional" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:conditional">5</a>–<a href="#sec:transport" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:transport">7</a> associate positive operators to partitions of the full system and interpolate between them as a small subsystem changes parts. These operators act on symmetric tensor powers, whose vectors are fixed by every permutation of the copies. Applying an inverse power of the interpolating operator to a vector built from ground-state copies and an auxiliary entangled pair defines the filtered vector whose norm we study. As the copy number grows, logarithmic norms per copy can be compared with combinations of marginal entropies. The decrease of a suitable logarithmic squared norm is bounded below by averaged conditional mutual information, up to a small error. The same transported states bound the energy cost. This common control permits a comparison of information gained with excitation energy spent.

3.  *Compare the norms and scan a collar.* Section <a href="#sec:comparators" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:comparators">8</a> gives two bounds on the negative logarithm of the filtered vector’s norm. Auxiliary dimensions are chosen from a high-probability part of the target’s Schmidt spectrum. Projecting the target and an auxiliary system onto an entangled pair gives the upper bound. The lower bound uses the global gap: low physical energy forces most copies into the ground state. Section <a href="#sec:scanner" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:scanner">9</a> moves the partitions through a collar according to a finite randomized schedule. Each interaction is rarely split by a moving boundary, and the schedule supplies an interpolation with sufficiently low energy. The two norm bounds first improve the box exponent repeatedly; their sharper form then gives $$I_\Omega(A\cap T:\Lambda\setminus(A\cap T_L))
           \le Cn^{1-\varepsilon}.$$ Here $T$ is one of the finite unions of controlled rectangles and triangles specified in Definition <a href="#scanner:template" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="scanner:template">27</a>, $\varepsilon>0$ is fixed, and $T_L$ is the ambient sup-norm enlargement by $L=\lfloor n^{1-\varepsilon}\rfloor$. These targets and their allowed enlargements have $O(n)$ boundary edges. The entire finite physical and auxiliary system and schedule are fixed before the copy number tends to infinity.

4.  *Amplify the information bound.* Section <a href="#sec:amplification" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:amplification">10</a> uses typical spectral subspaces to construct a candidate operator for restoring a target moved to an auxiliary reference. Its norm is controlled by the collar information. A localized product of contractions derived from the positive constraints suppresses the excited component, and polar decomposition yields a unitary comparison near the target. This unitary leaves both the reference and the remote physical system untouched; comparison with a state in which they are independent bounds their original mutual information. Enlarging the collar by a sublinear radius makes the bound smaller than any prescribed inverse power of $n$.

5.  *Arrange the regions for entropy cancellation.* Section <a href="#sec:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:geometry">11</a> builds the two ordered families described above. The collar around each region avoids the complement of $A$ and all earlier regions of its own family. Narrow strips and recursive repairs at point contacts produce these separations for arbitrary cuts while leaving only $O(|\partial_\Lambda A|)$ sites uncovered. The information errors are summable over the regions, so the two entropy chains prove <a href="#eq:area-law" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:area-law">[eq:area-law]</a>.

<a id="sec:prelim"></a>
### Entropy and induced-graph locality

We record the finite-dimensional conventions and elementary uniform bounds used throughout the proof. Unless specified otherwise, entropies refer to the original ground vector $\Omega$. A changed state is shown by a subscript. Juxtaposition of disjoint systems denotes their tensor product or their union.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Entropy identities and continuity

For a density matrix $\rho$ on systems $D,E,F$, define $$S(D|E)_\rho=S(DE)_\rho-S(E)_\rho,
 \quad I(D:E)_\rho=S(D)_\rho+S(E)_\rho-S(DE)_\rho,$$ and $$I(D:F|E)_\rho=S(DE)_\rho+S(EF)_\rho-S(E)_\rho-S(DEF)_\rho.$$ We use strong subadditivity, $I(D:F|E)_\rho\ge0$, for normalized finite-dimensional density operators (Lieb and Ruskai 1973) <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[LiebRuskai1973](#ref-LiebRuskai1973)]. It implies that conditioning decreases conditional entropy and that discarding systems cannot increase mutual information. Subadditivity and purification give $|S(D|E)|\le\log\dim D$. For a pure state the entropies of complementary systems coincide. These facts also hold with empty regions, whose Hilbert spaces are the one-dimensional empty tensor product.

Write $h(u)=-u\log u-(1-u)\log(1-u)$ for binary entropy. The trace distance of two states is half the trace norm of their difference. The continuity estimate below uses the dimension-independent conditional entropy method of Alicki and Fannes (Alicki and Fannes 2004) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[AlickiFannes2004](#ref-AlickiFannes2004)], in Winter’s sharpened form (Winter 2016) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[Winter2016](#ref-Winter2016)].

<a id="stmt-lem-continuity"></a>
<div id="lem:continuity" class="lemma">

**Lemma 3** (Continuity with a fixed controlled system). *Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on finite-dimensional $D\otimes E$, and put $\delta=\tfrac12\lVert \rho-\sigma\rVert_1\le1$ and $d_D=\dim D$. Then <a id="eq:conditional-continuity"></a>$$\label{eq:conditional-continuity}
 |S(D|E)_\rho-S(D|E)_\sigma|
 \le2\delta\log d_D+(1+\delta)
                 h\left(\frac{\delta}{1+\delta}\right)
 \le C\sqrt\delta\log(e d_D).$$ The same estimates hold for $S(D)$ by making $E$ trivial. Summing the bounds for $S(D)$ and $S(D|E)$ therefore bounds the continuity cost for $I(D:E)$ in terms of $d_D$, independently of $\dim E$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-continuity"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-continuity</summary>

*Proof.* We include the mixture argument for the bound in (Winter 2016, Lemma 2) <a id="pm-cite-34"></a>[[Winter2016](#ref-Winter2016)]. If $\tau=\sum_j p_j\tau_j$, adding a classical register that records $j$ shows $$0\le S(D|E)_\tau-\sum_jp_jS(D|E)_{\tau_j}\le H(p).$$ For the lower bound, condition on that register and use strong subadditivity. For the upper bound, use the ordinary mixing upper bound on $S(DE)$ and concavity of $S(E)$. The ordinary bound follows by recording a duplicate of the classical register: its conditional entropy given $DE$ is nonnegative after this further conditioning.

If $\delta>0$, write the Jordan decomposition $\rho-\sigma=\delta(\tau_+-\tau_-)$, where $\tau_\pm$ are states. Then $$\frac{\rho+\delta\tau_-}{1+\delta}
 =\frac{\sigma+\delta\tau_+}{1+\delta}.$$ Apply the mixture bounds to both expressions and use $|S(D|E)_{\tau_+}-S(D|E)_{\tau_-}|\le2\log d_D$. This proves the first inequality.
